questions.enonce_markdown:
The SDLC is used to develop and implement an information system.

(a) State three activities in the analysis phase of the SDLC. (3 marks)

(b) Describe two conversion methods used to implement a system. For one of the methods given above, state one advantage and one disadvantage. (4 marks)

(c) Explain why feedback is important in the maintenance phase of the SDLC. (1 mark)

(d) Why is documentation necessary in each phase of the SDLC? (1 mark)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(a) Three activities of the analysis phase (3 marks)** (any three):

- Studying the existing system and its problems through fact finding (interviews, questionnaires, observation, examination of documents).
- Identifying and defining the user requirements of the new system.
- Carrying out a feasibility study (technical, economic, operational) and a cost-benefit analysis.
- Modelling the current system (data flow diagrams, flowcharts) and writing the requirements specification.

**(b) Two conversion (changeover) methods (4 marks).**

- **Direct changeover:** the old system is stopped and the new one is used from a fixed date. *Advantage:* it is the cheapest and fastest method. *Disadvantage:* it is risky, because if the new system fails there is no old system to go back to.
- **Parallel running:** the old and the new systems are run side by side for a period and their results are compared before the old one is abandoned. *Advantage:* it is the safest, since the old system is still available if the new one has errors. *Disadvantage:* it is costly and demands extra work, because all the work is done twice.

(Other methods: pilot conversion, in which the new system is first used in one branch or department, and phased conversion, in which the new system is introduced module by module. The advantage and the disadvantage are required for one method only.)

**(c) Feedback in the maintenance phase (1 mark).** Users' feedback (reports of errors, difficulties, new needs) shows whether the system still meets the requirements and tells the maintenance team what must be corrected, adapted or improved, so the system stays useful and the next version can be better.

**(d) Documentation in every phase (1 mark).** It records what has been decided and done in the phase (requirements, design, tests, user instructions), so that the next phases, the maintenance team and the users can understand, use and modify the system later, even if the original staff have left.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(a) Describe three functions of an operating system. (3 marks)

(b) Name and explain two types of operating system. (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(a) Three functions of an operating system (3 marks)** (any three):

- *Memory management:* it allocates main memory to programs and data and protects each program's area from the others.
- *Processor (process) management:* it schedules the programs so that the CPU is shared and several tasks can run (multitasking).
- *File management:* it creates, names, stores, copies, protects and retrieves files and folders on the storage devices.
- *Device management:* it controls input and output devices through their drivers.
- *User interface and security:* it lets the user communicate with the computer (command line or graphical interface) and controls access by user accounts and passwords.

**(b) Two types of operating system (2 marks)** (any two):

- *Multi-user operating system* (for example Linux or Windows Server): several users, each at a terminal, use the same computer at the same time, and the system shares the resources and protects each user's data.
- *Real-time operating system* (used in industrial control, aircraft, medical equipment): it responds to events within a guaranteed, very short time.
- *Single-user, single-task system* (for example MS-DOS): it allows one user to run one program at a time. Other types: batch, network and mobile operating systems (for example Android).

questions.enonce_markdown: Describe two advantages and one disadvantage of using UNICODE instead of using ASCII. (3 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Two advantages of Unicode (2 marks).**

- Unicode can represent the characters of almost all the world's writing systems (more than 100 000 characters, with 16 or more bits per character), including accents, Chinese, Arabic, mathematical symbols and emoji, whereas ASCII has only 128 characters (7 bits; 256 in extended 8-bit versions), enough for English only.
- It is one universal standard, so text in many languages can be stored and exchanged between different computers and programs without the characters being displayed wrongly; the first 128 Unicode codes are the same as ASCII, so it is compatible with ASCII text.

**One disadvantage (1 mark).** Each character needs more memory (2 bytes or more, against 1 byte in ASCII), so files are larger and take longer to store and transmit; it also needs more processing and software and fonts that support it.
